Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: In plants, growth is an irreversible permanent increase in size of an organ, its parts, or an individual cell, accompanied by metabolic processes at the expense of energy.

Statement II: Plants retain the capacity for unlimited growth throughout their life due to the presence of meristems at certain locations in their body.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Plant growth is a metabolic, energy-expending process that is uniquely indeterminate (open) because of localised meristems.

Step 2: Evaluation
Biological growth is defined as an irreversible permanent increase in size accompanied by anabolic and catabolic processes occurring at the expense of energy. Furthermore, plants retain the capacity for unlimited growth throughout their life because meristematic cells at specific locations can divide and self-perpetuate.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTHANDDEVELOPMENT_SB2_Q02 - Roles of apical and lateral meristems

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Root apical meristem and shoot apical meristem are responsible for secondary growth, causing an increase in the girth of plant organs.

Statement II: Vascular cambium and cork-cambium are responsible for primary growth and principally contribute to elongation along the plant axis.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Primary growth (elongation along the plant axis) and secondary growth (increase in girth) are carried out by distinct meristematic regions.

Step 2: Evaluation
Root apical meristem and shoot apical meristem are responsible for primary growth and axial elongation, not secondary growth. Conversely, the lateral meristems—vascular cambium and cork-cambium—appear later in life in dicots and gymnosperms and cause an increase in girth (secondary growth), not primary elongation.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect because the roles of apical meristems and lateral meristems are reversed.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTHANDDEVELOPMENT_SB2_Q03 - Cellular traits in meristematic and elongation phases

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Cells in the meristematic phase of growth are rich in protoplasm, possess large conspicuous nuclei, and have thin primary cellulosic walls with abundant plasmodesmatal connections.

Statement II: Cells in the phase of elongation lose their vacuoles and undergo secondary lignocellulosic wall thickening.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The meristematic, elongation, and maturation zones of a growing axis exhibit distinct anatomical and cellular properties.

Step 2: Evaluation
Constantly dividing cells in the meristematic phase are rich in protoplasm, have large conspicuous nuclei, and possess thin primary cellulosic walls with abundant plasmodesmatal connections. In contrast, cells in the phase of elongation are characterised by increased vacuolation, cell enlargement, and new cell wall deposition—they do not lose vacuoles or undergo secondary lignocellulosic wall thickening (which occurs during maturation/tracheary element differentiation).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The description of the meristematic phase is correct, whereas the description of the phase of elongation is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTHANDDEVELOPMENT_SB2_Q04 - Arithmetic division versus sigmoid growth curve

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: In arithmetic growth, following mitotic cell division, both daughter cells retain the ability to divide and continue dividing exponentially.

Statement II: In geometrical growth in a natural environment, plotting the parameter of growth against time yields a typical sigmoid or S-curve.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Arithmetic and geometrical growth differ in the mitotic fate of daughter cells and the resulting shape of the growth curve over time.

Step 2: Evaluation
In arithmetic growth, following mitotic cell division, only one daughter cell continues to divide while the other differentiates and matures, giving a linear curve. Retaining the ability to divide in both progeny cells occurs in geometrical growth. In a natural environment with limited nutrients, geometrical growth shows a lag phase, an exponential phase, and a stationary phase, yielding a typical sigmoid (S-shaped) curve.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The claim about arithmetic growth is incorrect, whereas the claim about geometrical growth producing a sigmoid curve is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTHANDDEVELOPMENT_SB2_Q05 - Efficiency index and relative growth rate comparison

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: In the exponential growth expression \(W_1 = W_0 e^{rt}\), \(r\) is the relative growth rate and is also referred to as the efficiency index.

Statement II: If two leaves of different initial sizes increase in surface area by the same absolute amount over a given time, they have the same absolute growth rate, but the leaf with the smaller initial area has a higher relative growth rate.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Relative growth rate expresses growth per unit time on a common basis (per unit initial parameter), serving as a measure of efficiency in producing new plant material.

Step 2: Evaluation
In \(W_1 = W_0 e^{rt}\), \(r\) is indeed the relative growth rate and measures the plant's ability to produce new material, termed the efficiency index. Furthermore, when two leaves increase by the same absolute area \(\Delta A\) in unit time, their absolute growth rates are identical, while relative growth rate \(\frac{\Delta A}{A_0}\) is inversely proportional to initial area \(A_0\), making it higher for the smaller leaf.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: During differentiation into a tracheary element, plant cells retain dense protoplasm and develop thin primary cellulosic walls.

Statement II: The formation of interfascicular cambium and cork cambium from fully differentiated parenchyma cells is an example of redifferentiation.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Differentiation, dedifferentiation, and redifferentiation represent sequential transitions in mitotic capacity and structural specialisation.

Step 2: Evaluation
To form a tracheary element, cells lose their protoplasm and develop strong, elastic, lignocellulosic secondary cell walls to conduct water under extreme tension. Additionally, the formation of interfascicular cambium and cork cambium from fully differentiated parenchyma cells is an example of dedifferentiation (regaining mitotic capacity), not redifferentiation.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: In cotton, coriander, and larkspur, leaves of the juvenile plant differ in shape from those in mature plants, illustrating developmental plasticity.

Statement II: In buttercup, the difference in shapes of leaves produced in air versus water is caused by differences between juvenile and mature phases rather than the environment.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Plasticity refers to plants following different developmental pathways in response to either phases of life or environmental conditions.

Step 2: Evaluation
Heterophylly in cotton, coriander, and larkspur occurs between juvenile and mature life phases, representing developmental plasticity. However, heterophylly in buttercup (air versus water leaves) represents heterophyllous development due to the environment, not juvenile versus mature phases.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The statement regarding cotton, coriander, and larkspur is correct, whereas the statement regarding buttercup is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTHANDDEVELOPMENT_SB2_Q08 - Grouping of plant growth promoters and ethylene

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Auxins, gibberellins, and abscisic acid together constitute the group of plant growth promoters.

Statement II: The gaseous plant growth regulator ethylene could fit into either growth promoters or inhibitors, though it is largely an inhibitor of growth activities.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Plant growth regulators are broadly grouped into growth promoters and growth inhibitors based on their physiological roles.

Step 2: Evaluation
Plant growth promoters include auxins, gibberellins, and cytokinins—not abscisic acid, which belongs to the growth-inhibiting group involved in dormancy, abscission, and stress responses. Meanwhile, the gaseous PGR ethylene could fit either group, though it is largely an inhibitor of growth activities.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The claim grouping abscisic acid with growth promoters is incorrect, whereas the description of ethylene is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTHANDDEVELOPMENT_SB2_Q09 - Discovery of auxin by Darwin and Went

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Charles Darwin and Francis Darwin concluded that the tip of the canary grass coleoptile was the site of a transmittable influence that caused phototropic bending of the entire coleoptile.

Statement II: F.W. Went isolated auxin from the tips of coleoptiles of oat seedlings.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Auxin was discovered through classic phototropism experiments on grass coleoptiles.

Step 2: Evaluation
Charles Darwin and Francis Darwin observed that canary grass coleoptiles bent toward unilateral illumination and concluded that the tip was the site of a transmittable influence. Subsequently, F.W. Went isolated auxin from the tips of coleoptiles of oat seedlings.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTHANDDEVELOPMENT_SB2_Q10 - Discovery of gibberellic acid and kinetin

questiontext.text:

Statement I: The 'bakanae' disease of rice seedlings was caused by a bacterial pathogen, and its symptoms were reproduced by applying kinetin.

Statement II: Auxin was first crystallised from autoclaved herring sperm DNA by Miller et al. in 1955.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The discoveries of gibberellic acid and kinetin involved distinct biological sources and researchers.

Step 2: Evaluation
The 'bakanae' (foolish seedling) disease of rice was caused by the fungal pathogen Gibberella fujikuroi (not a bacterium), and E. Kurosawa reproduced its symptoms with sterile fungal filtrates containing gibberellic acid (not kinetin). Moreover, Miller et al. (1955) crystallised kinetin (not auxin) from autoclaved herring sperm DNA.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Removal of shoot tips (decapitation) overcomes apical dominance and promotes the growth of lateral buds, which is widely applied in tea plantations and hedge-making.

Statement II: The synthetic auxin 2,4-D selectively kills monocotyledonous weeds while leaving mature dicotyledonous lawn plants unaffected.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Auxins regulate apical dominance and are also used as selective herbicides in horticulture.

Step 2: Evaluation
Decapitation removes the growing apical bud, releasing lateral buds from apical dominance and promoting branching, which is widely used in tea plantations and hedge-making. However, 2,4-D selectively kills dicotyledonous weeds and does not affect mature monocotyledonous plants (such as lawn grasses), making the second claim reversed.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The statement about decapitation and apical dominance is correct, whereas the statement about 2,4-D selectivity is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTHANDDEVELOPMENT_SB2_Q12 - Gibberellin acidity senescence and sugarcane yield

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: All gibberellins are basic in nature and accelerate leaf and fruit senescence to shorten the market period of apples.

Statement II: Spraying sugarcane crops with gibberellins increases stem length and can increase yield by as much as 20 tonnes per acre.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Gibberellins are acidic plant growth promoters that stimulate axis elongation and delay senescence.

Step 2: Evaluation
All gibberellins are acidic (not basic), and they delay senescence (not accelerate it) so fruits can be left on the tree longer to extend the market period. On the other hand, spraying sugarcane crops with gibberellins increases the length of the sugar-storing stem, increasing yield by up to 20 tonnes per acre.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The claim about gibberellins being basic and accelerating senescence is incorrect, whereas the claim about increasing sugarcane yield is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTHANDDEVELOPMENT_SB2_Q13 - Kinetin versus zeatin and cytokinin functions

questiontext.text:

Statement I: Kinetin does not occur naturally in plants, whereas zeatin is a naturally occurring cytokinin isolated from corn-kernels and coconut milk.

Statement II: Cytokinins help overcome apical dominance and promote nutrient mobilisation, which helps delay leaf senescence.

Cytokinins promote cytokinesis, shoot formation, and nutrient mobilisation while counteracting apical dominance.

Step 2: Evaluation
Kinetin was obtained from autoclaved herring sperm DNA and does not occur naturally in plants, whereas zeatin is a natural cytokinin isolated from corn-kernels and coconut milk. Additionally, cytokinins help overcome apical dominance and promote nutrient mobilisation, delaying leaf senescence.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTHANDDEVELOPMENT_SB2_Q14 - Physiological roles of ethylene and ethephon

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Ethylene inhibits root growth and root hair formation, thereby reducing the absorption surface of plants.

Statement II: Ethephon suppresses female flower formation in cucumbers and delays fruit ripening in tomatoes and apples.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Ethylene and its aqueous source ethephon promote root hair formation, fruit ripening, and female flower development in cucurbits.

Step 2: Evaluation
Ethylene promotes (not inhibits) root growth and root hair formation, helping plants increase their absorption surface. Likewise, ethephon promotes (not suppresses) female flowers in cucumbers to increase yield and hastens (not delays) fruit ripening in tomatoes and apples.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Both statements are incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_PLANTGROWTHANDDEVELOPMENT_SB2_Q15 - Abscisic acid stress response and GA antagonism

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: Abscisic acid stimulates the closure of stomata and increases plant tolerance to various stresses, earning it the name stress hormone.

Statement II: In most physiological situations, abscisic acid acts synergistically with gibberellins to promote seed germination.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Abscisic acid (ABA) is a general plant growth inhibitor that mediates stress tolerance and seed dormancy.

Step 2: Evaluation
ABA stimulates stomatal closure and increases tolerance to stresses, which is why it is called the stress hormone. However, ABA inhibits seed germination and acts as an antagonist (not synergist) to gibberellins in most situations.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The description of ABA as a stress hormone is correct, whereas the claim that ABA acts synergistically with gibberellins is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

questiontext.text:
Read the following two statements carefully and select the correct option:

Statement I: In photoperiodism, shoot apices themselves directly perceive the relative durations of light and dark periods without any involvement of leaves.

Statement II: Vernalisation promotes flowering by exposure to a period of low temperature, preventing precocious reproductive development late in the growing season.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Light duration (photoperiodism) and low temperature (vernalisation) are key extrinsic factors regulating flowering.

Step 2: Evaluation
Shoot apices by themselves cannot perceive photoperiods; the site of perception of light and dark durations is the leaves, from which a hormonal substance migrates to shoot apices to induce flowering. Meanwhile, vernalisation refers to the promotion of flowering by a period of low temperature, preventing precocious reproductive development late in the growing season and allowing the plant sufficient time to reach maturity.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The claim about shoot apices perceiving photoperiods directly is incorrect, whereas the description of vernalisation is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct, but Statement II is incorrect.
